Chapter 00 · User book

Start here

A practical field guide for your personal Mac build.

Install once, add the keyer in Fusion, choose the input encoding, then inspect the matte. The GPU engine starts automatically.

Release status

This personal beta is under qualification. Read the acceptance report (in the original delivery folder) for the delivered installer. Native 1080p has completed real MPS and Resolve tests. Clean-account installation, whole-Mac offline first use, and restart checks still need their recorded physical handoff. Keep important work backed up and review your exports.

01Install02Make a key07Cache for playback08Export

What you need

An Apple Silicon Mac, sufficient local storage, DaVinci Resolve Studio, the offline installer and a short test shot. The measured machine is an M5 Pro with 48 GB memory, macOS 26.3.2 and Resolve Studio 21.1.1 build 10. Other machines and versions need their own qualification.

The installer contains the private runtime and models. Normal use needs no Python, model download, Terminal window or manually started worker. The Manager is optional maintenance.

How to read this book

Use the bookmarks on the left, the chapter links below each page, or your browser’s Find command. Every screenshot is an actual capture from this Mac. Some show the historical test-project name; the effect to add is always CorridorKey2.0 hp beta. Click a screenshot to inspect it. Print / Save PDF creates a paper-friendly book.

Chapter 01 · User book

Install and verify

Use the normal macOS Installer flow.

  1. Save your work and quit DaVinci Resolve and Fusion.
  2. Open the delivered CorridorKeyMac-…-arm64-Offline.pkg.
  3. Choose the startup disk and continue. Approve the normal macOS administrator prompt locally.
  4. Wait for The installation was successful, then close Installer.
  5. Open CorridorKey Mac Manager (window: CorridorKey2.0 hp beta Manager) in Applications and click Verify. A successful inventory check confirms installed files; GPU inference is checked separately on first use.
  6. Reopen Resolve. Keep the offline package somewhere safe for repair.

This private package is unsigned and its executable code is ad-hoc signed. It is not notarized. Use the normal macOS trust flow if requested; do not disable system protections.

If installation stops

Close Resolve and Fusion before retrying. Check free disk space: installation needs room for staging and rollback as well as installed assets. Unsupported destinations are refused. Do not move individual runtime or model folders.

Chapter 02 · User book

Make your first key

Start with a short copy of a shot.

  1. Put a green- or blue-screen clip on a timeline and open its Fusion page.
  2. Select the source node. Press Shift + Space, search for CorridorKey, select CorridorKey2.0 hp beta, and click Add.
  3. Confirm the flow: MediaIn → CorridorKey → MediaOut. Put any required color transform before the keyer.
  4. Select the keyer and open Inspector → Controls. Choose the actual Input Encoding described in the next chapter.
  5. Leave Mode: Single Frame, Output: Premultiplied, and Despill Amount: 0 for the first inspection. Leave hints unused for ordinary opaque camera footage.
  6. View the result. First use loads the models and performs a real GPU check before processing your frame. Allow it to finish.

An inference error stops the render and reports a problem. It does not silently substitute the original source. Original is an explicit preview choice.

← Install and verifySet color and resolution →
Chapter 03 · User book

Set color and resolution

Match the image arriving at the node.

Input EncodingUse when the node receives
sRGBsRGB transfer curve with sRGB / Rec.709 primaries.
Scene-linear Rec.709Linear RGB with Rec.709 / sRGB primaries.
Rec.709 Gamma 2.4A gamma 2.4 display image with Rec.709 primaries.

Choose the encoding after upstream transforms. A camera label alone is insufficient. Convert S-Log3 / S-Gamut, DaVinci Wide Gamut, ACES, PQ or HLG deliberately before the keyer. Gamma 2.4 is not the Rec.709 camera OETF. There is no automatic color-space detection.

Internal Resolution

Full runs at the node’s canvas size. Two Thirds, Half and Quarter calculate a smaller key and upscale it to that canvas. These are visible quality choices, saved in the project.

This beta refuses internal dimensions above 2048 × 1152. For a 3840 × 2160 source, Half explicitly calculates at 1920 × 1080. Native UHD failed quality qualification and is not supported by a Full claim. No failed Full render is automatically downgraded.

  1. Use Half or Quarter while adjusting the shot.
  2. For a native 1080p final, return to Full before analysis and export.
  3. For a larger canvas, choose a supported profile explicitly and inspect the upscaled edges at 100%.
Composition canvas

Resolve’s project resolution alone may not resize MediaIn in Fusion. Check the dimensions arriving at the keyer; insert an explicit resize before it when qualifying a 1920 × 1080 key.

Chapter 04 · User book

Inspect and composite

Check edges before judging the finished shot.

  1. In Output, select Matte. Inspect hair, gaps, motion blur and semi-transparent objects across several frames.
  2. Select Straight FG to inspect recovered foreground color without alpha multiplication.
  3. Return to Premultiplied for compositing and alpha export.
  4. Add a Merge. Connect the keyer to its foreground input and your replacement background to its background input. Connect Merge to MediaOut.
  5. Inspect over black, white and a saturated background at 100%. Check for edge halos, missing detail and spill.
Source → Keyer↓ Foreground
Merge → MediaOut
↑ BackgroundReplacement background

Premultiplied already associates RGB with alpha once. Do not multiply it again. Matte, Straight FG and Original are opaque inspection outputs and are not alpha-bearing final keys.

Output controlPurpose
White PointRemaps alpha, clamped to 0–1. The neutral value is 1. Inspect thin detail after changes.
Keep Solid DetailRestores original RGB where raw model alpha exceeds 0.95, before additional despill.
Linear OutputReturns scene-linear RGB; alpha is unchanged. Match downstream color handling.
Show ResultOff selects Original; on selects Premultiplied. It changes the saved output choice.

For linear-light compositing, feed scene-linear Rec.709 into the keyer and keep the Merge in the same linear representation. A checkerboard demonstrates transparency, not correct compositing by itself.

Chapter 05 · User book

Analyze a continuous shot

Temporal processing needs an exact range and stable inputs.

  1. Finish upstream retiming, resize and color decisions. Bake variable or fractional retiming first.
  2. Set Shot Start and Shot End to inclusive integer frames at this node. For 60 frames starting at 0, use 0 and 59. Include one continuous shot, with no cut.
  3. Open Time Awareness, select Mode: Temporal, and begin with Window: 4.
  4. Set the final Internal Resolution before analysis. Click Analyze Shot to advance the saved analysis revision.
  5. Let Resolve acquire the shot. A capture-verification message may ask you to render again. Keep upstream settings unchanged. Move the playhead one frame and back, or repeat the native pre-render, to verify the same input set. Do not click Analyze Shot again just to acknowledge this prompt: that advances another revision.
  6. Wait for the actual analysis to finish before playback or export. Review beginning, middle, end and fast motion.
Capture safety checked in 0.9.7

The installed 0.9.7 test rejected a source edit during acquisition and produced an exact stable retry. New or changed shots require two matching captures in separate render requests. Keep source, grade, hints and timing stable during analysis. A verification prompt is not a finished key.

The range is 2–240 frames. Shot End −1 uses the available source range; set an explicit end for predictable analysis. Split longer footage into continuous ranges. Node-input frame numbers can differ from timeline timecode, especially after trims or offsets.

Memory and window controls

ControlMeaning
WindowActual temporal context. Default 4 uses overlapping 4-frame windows with a 2-frame stride. Larger settings need more memory and separate validation.
GPU LimitAllocator ceiling relative to Metal’s recommended working set. Auto uses 80%; it does not report currently free RAM.
Low GPU MemoryUses smaller equivalent execution chunks. It preserves selected resolution, temporal window and float32 precision.
Reuse CapturesReuses verified input captures across explicit reanalysis. Unchanged playback already reuses captures.
CancelCancels this node’s wait. Resolve’s render cancel is the tested responsive host path. An already executing GPU operation can take time to finish.

Source and hint changes invalidate their dependent outputs. Analyze Shot also advances a saved render revision so the host can refresh its own cached output. Always refill playback cache after creative changes.

Chapter 06 · User book

Refine hints and despill

Start with the model result; add guidance only when useful.

Supply a useful hint

  1. Create a rough, aligned subject matte that retains the original RGB.
  2. Choose Source Alpha if the matte is carried in Source alpha, or connect a separate RGBA Hint input and choose Hint Alpha or Hint Luma.
  3. Keep the Hint’s dimensions, origin and timing identical to Source. Enable Use Hint.
  4. Adjust Hint Strength; new nodes start at 0.75. Compare with Use Hint off.

An ordinary camera clip with alpha 1 everywhere is not a useful subject hint. None / Legacy preserves saved-project behavior; leave Legacy Alpha off unless intentionally using that older switch.

Hint Frames: All Frames consumes each aligned hint. Reference Frame uses a chosen integer frame and propagates in Temporal mode, with Window 2 or higher. Leave Reference Frame blank to use Shot Start, type an in-range integer, or click Set Reference at that frame. A later reference propagates outward in both directions; inspect that variant separately. Internal Hint controls trust in the neural hint carried between windows, independently of your external matte.

Reduce remaining screen color

  1. Begin at Despill Amount: 0. The model already recovers foreground color.
  2. Increase Amount gradually while watching skin, fabric and transparent edges.
  3. Use Auto, Green, Blue or Picked for the additional correction. Auto estimates the backing from predicted-background pixels.
  4. Choose Average, Double Limit or Neutral, then compare against the uncorrected frame.

Freeze Color copies the last completed render’s detected backing into Picked Color and selects Picked. Render a key first. These controls are post-processing; they do not select a different neural model.

Chapter 07 · User book

Get smooth playback

Pre-render the key; live full-model processing is an offline operation.

Full 1080p neural inference is around 3 seconds per distinct Single Frame on the measured Mac. Smooth playback comes from a completed Resolve cache.

Fusion viewer: Cache to Disk

  1. Finish the shot’s settings and analysis. Set the composition render range to the shot.
  2. Right-click the keyer node and choose Cache to Disk.
  3. Enable caching and choose a writable local path ending in DiskCache0000.raw. Create the parent folder first if needed.
  4. Leave Lock Cache, Lock Branch and Use Network off.
  5. Click Pre-render and wait for every frame. If capture verification stops the first pass, repeat after checking the message.
  6. Play after completion. After any source or key change, let the unlocked cache invalidate and refill.

The actual installed 0.9.7 test reached 24.68 fps in a 25 fps Fusion project after native disk caching. Historical live temporal viewing with plugin results already cached was only about 1.6–1.9 fps because the host still acquired the shot. These are different measurements.

Edit timeline: User render cache

  1. Choose Playback → Render Cache → User.
  2. Right-click the timeline clip and choose Render Cache Fusion Output → On.
  3. Leave Resolve idle until the cache bar becomes blue, then play.

Practical speed choices

Use explicit Half or Quarter while adjusting edges, shorten the selected range, and avoid unnecessary reanalysis. Return to your intended final profile and refill cache before export. Preview settings are saved; they do not switch back automatically.

Final precision

Resolve’s playback cache is separate from the plugin’s float32 result cache. Leave Use render cached images off for a precision-critical final unless that Resolve cache format has been qualified for your HDR / alpha requirements.

Chapter 08 · User book

Export the final result

Choose whether you need a transparent key or a finished composite.

  1. Inspect the intended final Internal Resolution, input encoding, hint settings, shot range and Output. Reanalyze and refill any invalidated cache.
  2. For transparent output, connect the keyer’s Premultiplied output to MediaOut. For a finished replacement background, connect Merge to MediaOut instead.
  3. Open Deliver, choose Custom Export, and set the intended frame range and resolution.
  4. For a floating-point alpha master, choose EXR, RGBA (float 32), and enable Export Alpha. Set compression and destination as needed.
  5. For a movie with alpha, use an alpha-capable codec such as ProRes 4444 and enable Export Alpha. Confirm the available codec settings in your Resolve version.
  6. In Advanced Settings, leave Use render cached images off for the unqualified cache-format route.
  7. Add to Render Queue and start the job. Wait for Completed, then reimport and inspect the exported alpha, frame count, timing and several edges.

A black viewer background alone does not mean alpha is missing. Inspect alpha or composite the reimport over another background. H.264 / H.265 are not the demonstrated transparent-master route.

Actual native tests exported 60-frame Single Frame and Temporal EXR sequences, plus a 12-frame 30000/1001 ProRes 4444 alpha movie across a cut with independent keyers. The acceptance report records exact build identity and comparisons.

Chapter 09 · User book

Verify, repair and storage

Use the Manager when maintenance is needed.

Manager actionWhat to do
VerifyChecks the installed inventory. A file-integrity success is separate from inference and visual qualification.
GPU statusPrepares the real engine and reports loading, actual device, completed model work and errors.
Release GPUReleases an idle engine. The next render restarts it automatically. Active work blocks unsafe maintenance.
Storage / Open CacheShows storage use or opens this user’s product cache.
Choose Cache…Selects a writable cache location for this user, safely draining an idle engine first. Reconnect an unavailable cache volume or choose another.
Support FileCreates local diagnostic metadata without media, tokens or automatic uploads.
Repair…Select the matching offline installer; the Manager verifies its payload and executable installer logic before opening Installer.

Repair a missing or corrupt file

  1. Save your work and quit Resolve and Fusion.
  2. Open Manager and click Verify; retain the error details.
  3. Click Repair… and locate the matching delivered offline package, including if you moved it.
  4. Wait for complete package verification, then approve normal Installer authorization.
  5. After installation, run Verify again and reopen your test project.

Do not edit signed runtime files or move model folders by hand. Clear Shot Cache removes this node’s unshared captures/results; shared entries are retained. A cold render rebuilds missing cache data.

Chapter 10 · User book

Uninstall safely

Remove this product through the installed workflow.

  1. Save your projects and quit Resolve and Fusion.
  2. Open CorridorKey Mac Manager (window: CorridorKey2.0 hp beta Manager).
  3. Choose Keep Models to retain the shared model set for reinstall, or Remove All to remove this product’s models too.
  4. Approve the normal macOS Installer prompt and wait for completion.
  5. Reopen Resolve and check that the hp beta effect is absent from newly added effects. Saved nodes may appear unavailable until you reinstall.

The installed removal packages live in /Library/Application Support/HarvestPictures/CorridorKeyMac/Maintenance/. The delivered folder also contains both uninstall packages. Removal does not require the original downloaded offline installer.

The scoped removal targets this product’s plugin, Manager and runtime. It preserves the official CorridorKey plugin, other OFX plugins, source footage and Resolve projects. Per-user reconstructable cache is separate; after closing all engines, use Manager’s Open Cache location to identify product cache rather than deleting Resolve’s general CacheClip folder.

Qualification record

The installed 0.9.7 Manager passed graphical missing-file repair, interrupted-component recovery, Keep Models and Remove All tests. The final package was then reinstalled and fresh MPS inference verified. Read QA-37 and QA-38 in the accompanying report for the exact scope.

Chapter 11 · User book

Troubleshooting and limits

Follow the reported state; preserve the original footage.

SymptomNext step
Effect absentReopen Resolve after installation. Run Manager Verify. Search the exact hp beta name; the official effect has a separate entry.
First render takes timeCheck GPU status. Models load and a real GPU check precedes your first frame. Subsequent frames still take offline processing time.
Playback is very slowFollow the native Cache to Disk workflow in chapter 07; wait for all frames. Use explicit preview profiles while adjusting.
Capture verification promptKeep upstream settings unchanged and request another frame, or repeat pre-render. Resolve can refresh source identities after analysis; a safe rejection needs another render after it settles. Repeated Analyze Shot clicks create new revisions.
Memory errorClose unnecessary GPU-heavy work. Choose a lower Internal Resolution or a shorter validated window explicitly. Reinspect quality.
Unsupported internal sizeChoose Half / Quarter or resize before the keyer. Native UHD Full is unqualified.
Halo / wrong colorCheck input transfer function and primaries, premultiplication, downstream transforms and despill. Review over black and white.
Opaque alpha exportUse Premultiplied output, an alpha-capable format, and Export Alpha. Matte / Straight FG / Original are opaque previews.
Maintenance blockedFinish or cancel active work, save, then close Resolve and Fusion. Do not kill unrelated processes.
Cache volume unavailableReconnect it or use Choose Cache. Errors are explicit; do not replace private folders with loose symlinks.

Limits to keep in view

Live full-model playback is not real time. Larger windows, new memory profiles, other Macs, other host versions and transferred-package trust paths need their own checks. No automatic CPU neural fallback or automatic final-quality reduction is provided. Glass, blur and fine detail need shot-specific review; no arbitrary-footage perfect-matte promise is made.

Keep this book with NATIVE_QUALIFICATION.md (in the original delivery folder), PERFORMANCE.md (in the original delivery folder), KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md (in the original delivery folder), the checksums, source and installer. These local files contain the actual release scope.
